Section 2

Cosmological Background and Photon Trajectories

Before deriving the optical depth and transmitted flux, we must first specify the background spacetime in which the photons propagate. The absorption process that will be studied later does not occur in a static medium: photons travel through an expanding universe, and the gas elements that absorb them are encountered at different cosmological epochs along the line of sight. It is therefore necessary to establish how position along a photon trajectory is related to the cosmological evolution of the Universe. This section introduces that geometric background and derives the basic relation that governs the evolution of the scale factor along the ray.
